findings.title: Preserve source whitespace in exact citation exports
findings.trigger: A valid verified assessment citation contains line breaks, CRLF, tabs or indentation-sensitive code.
findings.impact: The fields explicitly labeled Exact source excerpt replace newline/CR/tab with spaces in Markdown and HTML. PDF derives from that Markdown and further collapses spaces. Consumers cannot copy or inspect the verified excerpt faithfully; Python/block and string-literal semantics can change while source byte offsets still name the original bytes.
findings.evidence: Exact extracted production text helpers reproduced with benign Python quote: if authorized:\n\tdelete_records()\nreturn ok -> one-line excerpt. Source call sites pass VerifiedCitation::quote through field/markdown_text and field/html_text.

reproduction.limitation: Standalone Rust harness extracts production helper bodies; privacy guard stubbed false for benign fixture. Does not run full renderer, approval chain or live service.

findings.remediation: Use a dedicated escaped verbatim source block for citations in Markdown/HTML and preserve line structure in PDF; verify exported multiline/tabs/CRLF quotes against the original admitted bytes or an explicitly documented visible encoding.

findings.title: Reject retry while the original shell attempt is still running
findings.trigger: Invoke review shell retry from another terminal while shell start has persisted Incomplete and is still waiting for a provider response; do not cancel first.
findings.impact: active_attempt_settled treats Incomplete as settled, allowing active_attempt to advance. The original evidence Store lock makes the new attempt fail store_busy; shell now points at failed attempt 2 while attempt 1 continues. A subsequent cancel writes attempts/2/cancel-request.json, not attempt 1's watched path. Original completion also cannot repair overall status because run_attempt only updates it when active_attempt equals its own attempt.
findings.evidence: Exact extracted settlement predicate returns true for Incomplete with neither run.json nor settlement.json. Followed retry, run_from_store Store lifetime, cancel_review and late run_attempt completion paths. Existing tests cover immediate retry after Cancelled but not directly during Incomplete.

reproduction.limitation: No provider calls, no full concurrent installed CLI execution; harness invokes extracted predicate over lightweight matching state types.

findings.remediation: Require a terminal, retained settlement before changing active_attempt; serialize/recheck shell state across retry/cancel/completion. Regression should hold first provider call, request retry directly, reject it, then verify cancellation still targets attempt 1.

retracted_candidates.title: Restore a finite response deadline for GitHub acquisition
retracted_candidates.trigger: GitHub accepts TCP/TLS but stalls response headers or stops sending the declared body. CLI GitHub acquisition calls the blocking transport directly.
retracted_candidates.impact: The acquisition can wait indefinitely and never produce its controlled failure or partial-state outcome. Request-count and byte bounds only advance as requests/bytes arrive; the connection timeout does not cover an already-connected stalled HTTP response.
evidence: Client builder explicitly sets timeout(None), leaving only connect_timeout(5 seconds). send() and read_to_end() have no enclosing deadline or cancellation.
git log -L 81,85:adl/src/codefriend/ingestion/github.rs confirms cb95ba8738 (#1102) replaced timeout(Duration::from_secs(20)) with timeout(None).

reproduction.limitation: No live or loopback network reproduction executed. Exact configuration and blocking call path inspected; existing prior finite timeout removal verified from commit diff.

retracted_candidates.remediation: Restore a finite total request deadline covering headers and body; add a controlled stalled-header and stalled-body fixture regression with a bounded elapsed-time assertion.
retracted_candidates.reason: GITHUB_INGESTION.md explicitly documents no total capture/request-duration cutoff under #1102. No separate required inactivity/cancellation contract established. Original remediation would contradict intended behavior; retain only as optional design question, not actionable defect.
